title: Personal Credit Cards: Redemption Minimums, Point Values and Redemption Options
content:
This reference gives, for each tier of Personal Credit Cards, the smallest number of points that may be redeemed at once, the dollar worth of one point for cash-type uses and for travel booked through the rewards center, the ways points may be used, and the delinquency level at which unredeemed points are lost.

| Tier | Smallest redemption | Worth of one point for cash-type uses | Worth of one point for travel through the rewards center | Ways points may be used | Delinquency, in days past due, that wipes out unredeemed points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable | none | not applicable |
| College Rewards Visa | 2500 points | 0.01 USD | not applicable | statement credit; deposit to checking; deposit to savings | 60 |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable | none | not applicable |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 2500 points | 0.01 USD | not applicable | statement credit; deposit to checking; deposit to savings | 60 |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 5000 points | 0.01 USD | 0.0125 USD | statement credit; deposit to checking; deposit to savings; travel booking; gift card | 60 |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 5000 points | 0.01 USD | 0.015 USD | statement credit; deposit to checking; deposit to savings; travel booking; gift card | 60 |

## Points of judgement

- Cash-type uses are a statement credit, a deposit to a bank account and a gift card; all of them are valued at the cash worth per point. Only travel booked through the rewards center uses the travel worth.
- The travel worth exists only on the two points-currency tiers.

> Worked example with hypothetical figures: 7340 points taken as a statement credit on Travel Rewards Visa Signature are worth 7340 multiplied by 0.01 USD, which is 73.40 USD; the same points used for rewards-center travel are worth 7340 multiplied by 0.0125 USD, which is 91.75 USD.
